name: How much does an open-concept kitchen conversion cost in Los Angeles if a wall is load-bearing?

mainEntity.name: How much should I budget for an open-concept kitchen conversion in Los Angeles if the wall I want removed is load-bearing?
mainEntity.text: How much should I budget for an open-concept kitchen conversion in Los Angeles if the wall I want removed is load-bearing?

acceptedAnswer.text: If the wall is load-bearing, budget for more than just demolition. The real cost usually includes a structural engineer, permit plan check, temporary support during construction, a properly sized beam, framing repairs, drywall, flooring patching or replacement, and any electrical or plumbing rerouting hidden in the wall. In Los Angeles-area homes, that can move a project from a moderate remodel into a major renovation. The final number depends on span length, roof or second-floor loads, access, finish level, and whether the kitchen footprint also changes. The best way to estimate accurately is to confirm whether the wall is structural before design is finalized. If it is, get a site review, engineering input, and a line-item estimate that separates demolition, structural work, trades, and finishes. That prevents surprise costs later and helps compare bids apples-to-apples.
acceptedAnswer.description: A load-bearing wall conversion usually costs more because it needs engineering, temporary shoring, beam installation, inspections, and permit plan check. In Los Angeles, the total budget often rises far above a cosmetic kitchen remodel once structure, electrical, plumbing, flooring, and finish work are included.
